q: Advisor says win data proves temporary-law route was correct, so House nod unnecessary. Flaw?
options: Reverse-engineers success; nod still mandatory in six weeks
expl: Outcome cannot cure procedure; placement plus nod needed.
why: Analyst reasons backwards from result. Law demands forward approval.

q: Note says pardon is absolute favour, so half line hides review for corrupt reasons. Truth?
options: Half-truth; limited review for mala fide exists
expl: Epuru allows narrow review for irrelevant reasons.
why: Half quote hides exception. Full rule includes check.

q: Temporary-law urgency collides with House supremacy claim that shortcut is permanent. Resolve?
options: Urgency starts it, House approval decides survival
expl: Cross-rule: urgency justifies start, House decides life.
why: Two principles coexist. Start does not equal survival.

q: Chain: House adjourned -> shortcut law -> reassembly -> no approval in six weeks -> ?
options: Dies; fresh Bill needed in House
why: Chain breaks without nod. Continuity needs fresh law.

q: All look right: elected-only voters, return-once, 15% cap, six-week death. When tick all?
options: Only if all four match without false add-on
expl: All four true; extra false spoils all-correct.
why: Everything-correct needs each verified plus no hidden false.

q: 2023 women's quota operative only after census and delimitation. Lesson for shortcut-law life?
options: Big steps wait on gates like census or reassembly nod
expl: 106th waits for census; ordinance waits for House nod.
why: Constitution gates power. Waiting is design, not delay.

q: 2024 nine-judge view on public resources cited to claim pardon can seize property. Use?
options: No, ruling on directive scope, not mercy seizure
expl: 39(b) ruling on resources, not pardon power.
why: Unrelated ruling cannot expand mercy. Pardon test stays mala fide.

q: New criminal codes stress remand production and women safeguards. Claim: pardon shields vanish. Valid?
options: Invalid, codes add safeguards; mercy review stays
expl: BNSS strengthens procedure; Epuru review survives.
why: New safeguards support fairness. They do not erase mercy check.

q: AP has 26 districts since 2022. Claim: more districts mean more minister posts beyond cap. Valid?
options: No, cap tied to House strength, not districts
expl: Cap is 15% of House, not district count.
why: District reform aids admin. Minister ceiling follows House size.
trapnote: Do not link districts to cap.

q: Nov 2022 quota verdict upholding 10% EWS cited to claim defector bar is gone. Correct?
options: No, verdict on EWS validity, not anti-defection bar
expl: Janhit Abhiyan on reservation, not defector minister bar.
why: EWS validity does not touch 91st bar. Defector still needs re-election.
